## Stories

A story is one piece of work, written as it will be sent: a title, a prompt, and how it will be sent. Each is a row, 36 pixels tall: a drag grip at its left; a small mode picker, a pill reading its mode, "Code", "Chain", "Spec", "Ask", or "Freeform", in that mode's colour, as the [PromptModes](../prompt-mode/modes/index.md#prompt-modes) colours it; its title, in the body's text colour, cut off with an ellipsis; then, at its right, muted, a small icon for anything attached, and, once it has been sent, its status as a task's is shown. Hovering a row shows a small ghost "Send" button and a menu button at its right.
Clicking a row opens it beneath, expanded in place, the others moving down: its title, editable in place; its prompt, in a [GrowingTextInput](../../ui/components/growing-text-input/index.md#growing-text-input) with the chat input's highlighting, completions, and slicing, as the [ChatInput](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input) has, and its attachments beneath; and its parameters, its mode, model, effort, and Slice, as the chat input shows them. Every change is saved as it is made. Only one story is open at a time; Escape or clicking its row again closes it.

## Creating

Creating a story is quick. A "New story" line at the foot of each section, and Ctrl+N (Cmd+N on macOS) while Planning has focus, adds a story there, open, its title focused, in the mode last picked for a story. Typing a title and pressing Enter adds it and starts another beneath it, so a list can be written down without the mouse; Escape on an empty one removes it. A title with no prompt sends its title as its prompt.
A story can also be prompted into existence: "Draft stories", a button beside the Backlog's heading, opens a small box to say what is wanted, in a sentence or a paragraph, and asks the harness, in a run of its own with no session, with the planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts), to break it into stories, each with a title, a prompt, and the mode that fits it. They come back into the Backlog as drafts, marked with a small dot, in the order given, each to be kept, edited, or removed; a draft is a story like any other once it has been opened. While the run goes, the box shows a spinner, and one that fails says why. An Ask answer's prompt cards also offer "Add to backlog", which adds the card's prompt as a story in its mode.

## Sprint

Stories move between the Backlog and Next sprint by dragging, as the [DragReorderBehaviour](../../ui/behaviours/drag-reorder/index.md#drag-reorder-behaviour) says, across the sections as within them, or from a row's menu, "Move to next sprint" or "Move to backlog". Their order within Next sprint is the order they will be sent. A row's menu also has "Duplicate" and "Delete".
"Send sprint", a primary button at the right of Next sprint's heading, enabled while it holds a story, sends every story in it, in order, as though each had been written in the chat input on its mode's tab and sent, one after another, as the [PromptSending](../prompt-mode/sending/index.md#prompt-sending) says: each task queues in its lane behind the one before it, in the order of the sprint, and each question runs at once. The stories go into the queue as one block, so nothing sent later comes between them, and the queue's auto-send carries them on as ever, as the [QueueList](../prompt-mode/queue-list/index.md#queue-list) says. A story's own "Send" sends it alone the same way.
A story once sent stays in its section, its row showing its task's status as it queues, runs, and ends, and clicking it opens its task in the Tasks tab. Once every story of the sprint has ended, the section offers "Close sprint", which moves the stories that are done into a muted, collapsed "Done" list beneath the Backlog, and leaves any that failed or were cancelled in Next sprint, to be sent again.

## Saving

The stories, their order, and which section each is in are saved with the project's data, as the [ProjectData](../project-data/index.md#project-data) says, in `.suspense/planning/`, a file per story, holding its hidden anchor as a queued prompt's is, and an `order.json` listing the sections and their stories, so the plan is kept with the project and comes back as it was left.

## Layout

Everything in Planning is laid out on one rhythm, so it scans as a single list. The column has 24 pixels of padding at its top and sides. Each section's heading is a row 32 pixels tall: its name in small semibold text, its count beside it, muted, and its actions at its right, each a labelled button, never an icon alone; 8 pixels beneath it its first row. Story rows are 36 pixels tall, 2 pixels apart, each with 12 pixels of padding at either side, their parts in fixed columns, so the grips, mode pills, titles, and statuses line up down the whole list: the grip 16 pixels, the mode pill 72 pixels, the title the rest, the status and time right-aligned in a column of their own 96 pixels wide, then the row's buttons. Sections are 24 pixels apart. Every row's state reads the same way, as below, and every label is the same small text, muted where it is secondary.

## States

Each part of Planning has the same few states, shown the same way wherever they come up, so a state is never guessed from what is missing.
- Empty: a single muted line, centred in the section, saying what is missing and what to do, as "Nothing planned. Drag stories here, or press Ctrl+N.", with no illustration
- Loading: a spinner and a short muted label of what is happening, as "Drafting stories…", in the place the result will appear, never a blank space
- Paused: a story whose task is paused shows "Paused" as its status, in the theme's warning colour, with a small pause icon, and a "Resume" button in its row, as the PromptSending says of pausing; a sprint with any story paused says so in its heading, as "1 paused", in the same colour
- Error: a line in the theme's error colour, saying what went wrong in plain words, with what the harness or the application reported beneath it collapsed under "Details", and a "Try again" button where trying again can help
A story's status in its row is the same coloured label a task has, as the [MessageList](../prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list)'s status says, Queued, Running with its spinner and time, Done, Failed, Cancelled, or Paused, and a story not yet sent shows nothing there, so its absence means "not sent".

## Drafting

Drafting stories shows its work in one place, a panel opened beneath the Backlog's heading, never in a popup that hides the list. It has the request box at its top, labelled "Describe what you want", and beneath it, while the run goes, its research: a muted line of what the harness is doing, as "Reading the spec…", with its spinner, updating as it goes, and a "Stop" button. Once it ends, the panel lists the proposed stories, each a row as a story's is, with a checkbox at its left, all checked to start with, then "Add N stories" and "Discard" buttons along the panel's foot: adding moves the checked ones into the Backlog, in order, and closes the panel. A proposal can be opened and edited before it is added, as any story is. A run that fails shows its error, as the states say, and leaves the request in its box to try again; one that proposes nothing says so, as an empty state. Proposals are kept until added or discarded, so closing Planning and coming back finds them as they were.

## Keyboard

Everything in Planning can be done from the keyboard. Tab moves through the section headings' buttons, the rows, and the open story's fields in order, and the focused one shows the theme's focus ring. In a list, Up and Down move between rows, Enter opens or closes the focused story, Space toggles a proposal's checkbox, and Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the focused story up or down, across sections as dragging does. Ctrl+N adds a story, Ctrl+Enter sends the focused story, Ctrl+Shift+Enter sends the sprint, and M opens the focused story's mode picker, whose options are picked with the arrow keys and Enter. Delete deletes the focused story after a confirmation. Escape closes what is open, a menu, a story, or the drafting panel, one at a time. Every button and control has a label a screen reader reads, as its visible text or, for an icon, its tooltip, and each shortcut is given in the tooltip of the control it stands for.

content.text:
Planning now follows the spec's layout, states, drafting and keyboard sections. I added tests for empty sections, keyboard use, drafting proposals and a failed draft. They and the existing planning, sprint, ribbon and card tests pass (28 in all) in a scratch copy of the project, and clippy is clean for Planning. I haven't tried it in the running app.

As the spec step said, "research output", "pause state" and "task proposals" were taken to mean the Draft stories run, stories whose task is paused, and the drafted stories.

**What changed:**
- **Layout:** the spacing and fixed row columns follow the spec exactly, so pills, titles and statuses line up down the whole list. Section headings use only labelled buttons.
- **Status:** a sent story shows the same coloured label as a task, with a spinner and running time while it runs. A paused story shows "Paused" in the warning colour with a Resume button in its row, and the sprint's heading says "N paused". Unsent stories show nothing.
- **Empty and error states:** empty sections show one centred line, such as "Nothing planned. Drag stories here, or press Ctrl+N." A failed draft gives a plain-words error with collapsed Details and Try again, and keeps your request in the box.
- **Drafting:** it's now an inline panel under the Backlog heading with a "Describe what you want" box. Drafted stories come back as proposals with checkboxes and "Add N stories" / "Discard". Proposals are saved with the project, so they're still there after closing Planning.
- **Keyboard:**
  - Rows can be tabbed to and show a focus ring.
  - Up/Down move between rows, Enter opens or closes a story, and Space ticks a proposal.
  - Alt+Up/Down move a story, across the Next sprint/Backlog boundary too.
  - Ctrl+Enter sends a story and Ctrl+Shift+Enter sends the sprint.
  - M opens a mode picker you can use with the arrow keys.
  - Delete asks for confirmation in the row, and Escape closes one thing at a time.
  - Tooltips list the shortcuts.

**Two places it falls short of the spec:**
- **Progress line:** the drafting run gives no progress, so instead of a live line like "Reading the spec…" the panel shows "Asking the harness to break it into stories…" with a timer.
- **Stop:** it discards the result, but the harness run itself carries on in the background until it finishes.

The confirmation for Delete is a prompt in the row itself rather than a separate dialog.
